_note: SYNTHETIC — not a real sxp_activity_criteria row. Invented activity, supplier and city. Numbers are internally consistent: the two tag counts below sum to ts_tag_bookings, and the supplier tag rate clears the deck's bar. The activity does not exist.
_scenario: Trust & Safety failed on the TAG RATE alone — the third and last unexercised T&S state. No severe case (crit_ts_no_severe_case true) and the investigated-case rate is fine (crit_ts_case_rate true, 1 weighted case, below the '≥ 2 weighted cases' trigger), but 0.82% of the supplier's bookings carry a T&S tag against a > 0.5% bar, so the whole supplier is out. Everything else passes — entry, rating, quality defects — which makes this the cleanest illustration of the tag rule on its own.
_note_rule: Deck Gate 3 rule C: '> 0.5% of the supplier's bookings carry a T&S tag, with ≥ 2 tagged → supplier out'. Here 61 / 7,400 = 0.8243%. Unlike rules A and B this one is explainable to suppliers, because T&S tags are AI-classified review text rather than investigated cases — which is why this state shows a breakdown and the case-rate state (516:51696) deliberately shows none.
_note_details: NOT from the export. sxp_activity_criteria carries supplier_ts_tag_bookings as a bare count with no per-tag split, so the breakdown is hand-written. Tag names, descriptions and the advice list are transcribed from the design (Figma 516:52273); the two tags map to the real warehouse tags 'Accident Injury' and 'Aggressive Abusive Behaviour', both of which are in the 13 that drive this rule.
